title: Pexip Interoperability and Protocol Mix
exclusions: Covers the detection logic documented for 'Pexip Interoperability and Protocol Mix' only. Does not supplant cross-domain SIEM playbooks for unrelated domains or regulatory attestation. Entities listed in `operational_exceptions.csv` during approved tests are excluded.
evidence: Saved search `operations_pexip_interoperability_and_protocol_mix` (UC-11.3.58), SOC dashboard panel "Operations — Pexip Interoperability and Protocol Mix", and weekly export to `index=audit_evidence` sourcetype=csv:ops_controls.

controlTest.positiveScenario: Ingest synthetic events into `index=pexip` sourcetype='pexip:participant' that satisfy the UC-11.3.58 SPL filters for 'Pexip Interoperability and Protocol Mix'. Run the saved search and confirm at least one alertable row with expected fields populated.

dataSources: `sourcetype=pexip:participant` (polled from `/api/admin/history/v1/participant/`) Collected via Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617) modular input or scripted poll into the index named in the SPL.
app: Custom Pexip TA (scripted input polling Management REST API) — Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617)
spl:
index=pexip sourcetype="pexip:participant"
| eval protocol=coalesce(protocol, "Unknown")
| eval vendor=case(
    like(user_agent, "%Teams%") OR protocol="mssip", "Microsoft Teams",
    like(user_agent, "%Oand%") OR like(user_agent, "%webrtc%") OR protocol="webrtc", "WebRTC Browser",
    like(user_agent, "%Poly%") OR like(user_agent, "%OALTP%"), "Poly Endpoint",
    like(user_agent, "%Cisco%") OR like(user_agent, "%CE%"), "Cisco Endpoint",
    protocol="sip", "SIP (Other)",
    protocol="h323", "H.323 (Other)",
    1==1, "Other")
| bin _time span=1d
| stats count as participants, avg(call_quality) as avg_quality, dc(conference_name) as conferences by _time, protocol, vendor
| sort _time, -participants
description: Pexip's core value proposition is interoperability — connecting participants across SIP, H.323, WebRTC, Microsoft Teams, and Google Meet. Understanding the protocol mix reveals how the platform is actually being used versus its intended deployment. A shift from H.323 to WebRTC signals endpoint modernization. Growing Teams Connector traffic validates the hybrid meeting room investment. Protocol distribution also affects capacity planning because different protocols consume different amounts of transcoding resources on Conferencing Nodes.
value: Early 'Pexip Interoperability and Protocol Mix' detection reduces operational risk and delayed incident response by giving Operations operators a Splunk-native signal before manual triage or audit channels surface the issue.
implementation: Poll `/api/admin/history/v1/participant/` via the custom Pexip TA. Each participant record includes protocol, user_agent, call quality, and duration. Map user_agent strings to vendor categories using eval case logic. Track protocol distribution over time to identify migration trends (e.g., H.323 declining, WebRTC growing). Compare call quality by protocol and vendor — if Cisco endpoints consistently show higher quality than Poly endpoints, this informs procurement decisions. Generate monthly interoperability reports showing protocol mix, vendor distribution, and quality-by-protocol. This data also supports Pexip license negotiations by showing which features (Teams Connector, WebRTC gateway) drive the most value.
visualization: Pie chart (participant count by protocol), Stacked area chart (protocol distribution trend over 30 days), Table (vendor breakdown with quality metrics), Column chart (average quality by protocol).
dataModelAcceleration: Not applicable; primary SPL uses raw or vendor-normalized event fields.
knownFalsePositives:
1. **Scheduled maintenance** — Planned change generates expected deviations for 'Pexip Interoperability and Protocol Mix'. Cross-check change records.

2. **Batch job cycle** — Fixed-schedule workload skews `pexip` metrics.

3. **Monitoring synthetic checks** — Health probes from known hosts.

4. **Onboarding burst** — New entities produce atypical volume until baseline stabilizes.

**Suppression mechanism:** `ops_exception_register.csv` with entity, reason, valid_until.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
Run the following SPL in Search (then save as report or alert; adjust time range and threshold as needed):

```spl
index=pexip sourcetype="pexip:participant"
| eval protocol=coalesce(protocol, "Unknown")
| eval vendor=case(
    like(user_agent, "%Teams%") OR protocol="mssip", "Microsoft Teams",
    like(user_agent, "%Oand%") OR like(user_agent, "%webrtc%") OR protocol="webrtc", "WebRTC Browser",
    like(user_agent, "%Poly%") OR like(user_agent, "%OALTP%"), "Poly Endpoint",
    like(user_agent, "%Cisco%") OR like(user_agent, "%CE%"), "Cisco Endpoint",
    protocol="sip", "SIP (Other)",
    protocol="h323", "H.323 (Other)",
    1==1, "Other")
| bin _time span=1d
| stats count as participants, avg(call_quality) as avg_quality, dc(conference_name) as conferences by _time, protocol, vendor
| sort _time, -participants
```

**Pipeline walkthrough**

• Scopes the data: index=pexip, sourcetype="pexip:participant". Cross-check against **Data sources** above so indexes and sourcetypes match your ingestion.
• `eval` defines or adjusts **protocol** — often to normalize units, derive a ratio, or prepare for thresholds.
• `eval` defines or adjusts **vendor** — often to normalize units, derive a ratio, or prepare for thresholds.
• Discretizes time or numeric ranges with `bin`/`bucket`.
• `stats` rolls up events into metrics; results are split **by _time, protocol, vendor** so each row reflects one combination of those dimensions.
• Orders rows with `sort` — combine with `head`/`tail` for top-N patterns.
